cases.sentence: Точно ___ упал вдруг перед ним и заключил его в безвыходное и тяжелое уединение.
options: туман
тумана
туману
туманом
cases.translation: It was as if a fog had suddenly fallen before him and shut him into hopeless, oppressive isolation.
cases.explain: "Туман" is the subject of the verb "упал" (fell), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Он встречался со Свидригайловым почти всегда в квартире у ___, куда тот заходил как-то без цели.
options: Соня
Сони
Соне
Соней
cases.translation: He almost always ran into Svidrigailov at Sonya's apartment, which the man visited seemingly without any purpose.
cases.explain: The preposition "у" (at/by) always governs the genitive case, giving "Сони."

cases.sentence: Раскольников, как только вышел Разумихин, встал, повернулся к ___, толкнулся в угол, в другой.
options: окно
окна
окну
окном
cases.translation: As soon as Razumikhin left, Raskolnikov got up, turned toward the window, and moved from one corner to another.
cases.explain: The preposition "к" (toward) always governs the dative case, giving "окну."

cases.sentence: Даже раз он вышел в какую-то ___, но чем уединеннее было место, тем сильнее он сознавал что-то тяжелое.
options: роща
рощи
роще
рощу
cases.translation: Once he even wandered out into some grove, but the more isolated the place, the more strongly he felt something oppressive.
cases.explain: The preposition "в" expressing motion into a place governs the accusative case here, giving "рощу."

cases.sentence: Деньги тоже многому помогли, так как сирот с ___ поместили гораздо легче, чем сирот нищих.
options: капитал
капитала
капиталу
капиталом
cases.translation: Money also helped a great deal, since orphans with capital were placed far more easily than penniless orphans.
cases.explain: The preposition "с" (with) here governs the instrumental case, giving "капиталом."

cases.sentence: Он сидел в каком-то жалком ___ один, за столом, в размышлении.
options: трактир
трактира
трактиру
трактире
cases.translation: He sat alone in some wretched tavern, at a table, lost in thought.
cases.explain: The preposition "в" marking location governs the prepositional case, giving "трактире."

reading.ru: Для Раскольникова наступило странное время.
reading.question: How does the narrator describe the period that begins for Raskolnikov in this section?
options: A strange time, as if he were shut into oppressive isolation
A joyful and carefree time
A time of great wealth and success
A time of constant travel
reading.correct: A strange time, as if he were shut into oppressive isolation
reading.explain: The narrator says a strange time began for Raskolnikov, as though a fog had fallen and shut him into hopeless, oppressive isolation.

reading.ru: «Я тебе третьего дня, кажется, с сестрой говорил, Разумихин».
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov remind Razumikhin about in this exchange?
options: That he spoke with him and his sister two days earlier
That he owes Razumikhin money
That Razumikhin promised to visit Porfiry
That his mother is arriving soon
reading.correct: That he spoke with him and his sister two days earlier
reading.explain: Raskolnikov reminds Razumikhin that he believes he spoke with him, along with his sister, two days before.

reading.ru: Странно, он не очень удивился Порфирию и почти его не испугался.
reading.question: How does Raskolnikov react to Porfiry's unexpected appearance?
options: Strangely, he is not very surprised and barely frightened
He panics and tries to flee immediately
He bursts into tears
He attacks Porfiry physically
reading.correct: Strangely, he is not very surprised and barely frightened
reading.explain: The narrator notes it is strange that Raskolnikov is not very surprised by Porfiry and is barely frightened of him.

reading.ru: Потому тут дело жизни и смерти.
reading.question: What does the speaker emphasize is at stake in this conversation?
options: A matter of life and death
A matter of money only
A matter of simple curiosity
A matter of legal paperwork
reading.correct: A matter of life and death
reading.explain: The speaker stresses that this is a matter of life and death, underscoring the gravity of what is being discussed.

reading.ru: Решился, да как с горы точно упал, или из колокольни слетел.
reading.question: How does Porfiry describe the way Raskolnikov acted once he had decided on the crime?
options: As if he fell off a mountain or flew off a bell tower — sudden and reckless
Slowly and carefully planned over months
Accidentally, without ever really deciding
With the careful help of an accomplice
reading.correct: As if he fell off a mountain or flew off a bell tower — sudden and reckless
reading.explain: Porfiry describes the decision as sudden and headlong, "as if he'd fallen off a mountain or flown off a bell tower."

reading.ru: Может, вас Бог для чего и бережёт?
reading.question: What hopeful suggestion does the speaker make to Raskolnikov?
options: That God may be preserving him for some purpose
That the police have given up the investigation
That his mother will save him
That Sonya will marry him regardless
reading.correct: That God may be preserving him for some purpose
reading.explain: The speaker suggests that perhaps God is preserving Raskolnikov for some purpose, urging him to have courage.

reading.ru: От кого в Петербурге могла бы она получать письма?
reading.question: What question does Raskolnikov ask himself about a letter Dunya received?
options: Who in Petersburg could be writing to her
Why she was crying
Whether it contains money
Whether their mother wrote it
reading.correct: Who in Petersburg could be writing to her
reading.explain: Raskolnikov wonders from whom in Petersburg Dunya could possibly be receiving letters, immediately suspecting Luzhin.

reading.ru: Ну вот хотя бы эта бедная Катя, видели?»
reading.question: What modest meal does the speaker point to as an example of what he actually eats?
options: Leftover beefsteak and potatoes on a tin plate
A grand feast at a restaurant
Only bread and water
Fresh fish he caught himself
reading.correct: Leftover beefsteak and potatoes on a tin plate
reading.explain: He points to a corner where, on a small table on a tin plate, lie the remains of a wretched beefsteak with potatoes, as proof he is no gourmand.

reading.ru: Как же было пропустить такого нового и прекрасного друга?
reading.question: What does the speaker say about not wanting to miss out on someone new?
options: He couldn't pass up such a wonderful new friend
He wanted to avoid a new acquaintance entirely
He forgot the friend's name immediately
He refused to introduce the friend to anyone
reading.correct: He couldn't pass up such a wonderful new friend
reading.explain: The speaker remarks how could one possibly pass up such a splendid new friend, referring sarcastically to someone being gossiped about.

reading.ru: Опять уходить?» «Нет, я уже теперь не уйду».
reading.question: What does the speaker promise after being asked if he is leaving again?
options: That he will not leave now
That he will leave immediately
That he will return tomorrow
That he needs to think about it
reading.correct: That he will not leave now
reading.explain: Asked if he is leaving again, he answers firmly, "No, I won't leave now."

reading.ru: Сошли на тротуар. — Вам направо, а мне налево.
reading.question: What happens as the two characters part ways on the sidewalk?
options: One goes right while the other goes left
They continue walking together
They get into a carriage together
They argue about which way to go
reading.correct: One goes right while the other goes left
reading.explain: Stepping down onto the sidewalk, one says, "You go right, and I'll go left," as they part.

reading.ru: И в деревне вреда сделали больше вы мне, чем я вам.
reading.question: What accusation is made about who caused more harm in the countryside?
options: That the other person did more harm to the speaker than the speaker did to them
That no harm was done by either side
That a third party caused all the harm
That the harm was purely accidental
reading.correct: That the other person did more harm to the speaker than the speaker did to them
reading.explain: The speaker insists that in the countryside, the listener did him more harm than he did to them.

reading.ru: Тут была тоже одна собственная теорийка, так себе теория, по которой люди разделяются, видите ли, на материал и на особенных людей, то есть на таких людей, для которых по их высокому положению закон не писан, а напротив, которые сами сочиняют законы остальным людям, материалу-то, ссору-то.
reading.question: What theory does this passage describe, dividing people into two categories?
options: A theory dividing people into ordinary "material" and "extraordinary" people not bound by law
A theory about rich versus poor people
A theory about men versus women
A theory about city versus country dwellers
reading.correct: A theory dividing people into ordinary "material" and "extraordinary" people not bound by law
reading.explain: The passage describes Raskolnikov's own theory dividing humanity into ordinary "material" and "extraordinary" people, for whom, due to their exalted position, the law is not written.

reading.ru: Вы далеко совершеннолетняя и свой собственный рассудок имеете.
reading.question: What does the speaker point out about the woman's legal status and judgment?
options: That she is well of age and has her own good judgment
That she is still a minor and needs guardianship
That she has lost her mind
That she cannot make her own decisions
reading.correct: That she is well of age and has her own good judgment
reading.explain: The speaker points out that she is well past the age of majority and has her own sound judgment, so no one else can be blamed for her choices.

reading.ru: Затем, сунув деньги в карман, он хотел было переменить и на себе платье, но, посмотрев в окно и прислушавшись грозе, к дождю, махнул рукой, взял шляпу и вышел, не заперев квартиры.
reading.question: What does the man do after arriving home soaked to the skin, just before going out again to see Sonya?
options: He takes out all his money and tears up several papers
He calls a doctor immediately
He writes a long letter to the police
He burns all his furniture
reading.correct: He takes out all his money and tears up several papers
reading.explain: Having come home drenched, he locks himself in, opens his bureau, takes out all his money, and tears up two or three papers, before heading out again to see Sonya.

reading.ru: Оборванец, своротившийся с чаем из телятины, не мог удержаться, чтобы не спросить еще раз «Не надо ли еще чего-нибудь?» и, выслушав опять ответ отрицательный, удалился окончательно.
reading.question: What does Svidrigailov do with the tea and food that the ragged boy brings?
options: He drinks the tea to warm up but cannot eat anything, having lost his appetite
He eats everything hungrily
He gives it all to the boy
He throws it out the window
reading.correct: He drinks the tea to warm up but cannot eat anything, having lost his appetite
reading.explain: After the ragged boy finally leaves, Svidrigailov drinks the tea to warm himself but cannot eat a bite, having completely lost his appetite.

reading.ru: «Это точно румянец от вина, точно как будто ей дали выпить целый стакан.
reading.question: What does Svidrigailov think about the strange flush he sees in his vision?
options: That it looks like a flush from wine, as if she'd been given a whole glass to drink
That it is simply a sign of good health
That it is just makeup
That it means she is furious
reading.correct: That it looks like a flush from wine, as if she'd been given a whole glass to drink
reading.explain: Svidrigailov thinks the flush on the drowned girl's face in his vision looks exactly like the flush of wine, as though she had been given a whole glass to drink.

reading.ru: Про сестру уже не говорю, чтоб она уж так очень была ко мне непочтительна.
reading.question: What does the speaker say about his sister's attitude toward him?
options: That he won't even say she is very disrespectful toward him
That she adores him completely
That she has disowned him
That she wants him to move in with her
reading.correct: That he won't even say she is very disrespectful toward him
reading.explain: The speaker adds that he won't even claim his sister is so very disrespectful toward him, though he doesn't complain.

reading.ru: Раскольников горько усмехнулся.
reading.question: What bitter admission does Raskolnikov make with a bitter smile?
options: "I did not believe"
"I never loved her"
"I always knew the truth"
"I planned everything perfectly"
reading.correct: "I did not believe"
reading.explain: Raskolnikov smiles bitterly and admits, 'I did not believe,' right after 'Thank God' is said.

reading.ru: Они ждали вместе с Дуней.
reading.question: Why did the visitor come to see Sonya that morning?
options: Because she remembered Svidrigailov's words that Sonya knew about something important
Because she wanted to borrow money
Because she wanted to invite her to a wedding
Because she was lost and needed directions
reading.correct: Because she remembered Svidrigailov's words that Sonya knew about something important
reading.explain: She came to Sonya that morning after recalling Svidrigailov's words from the day before, that Sonya knew about the matter.

reading.ru: Вот этот толстый немец, должно быть, что толкнул меня.
reading.question: Who does the speaker blame for shoving him in the crowd?
options: A fat German man
A young boy
A policeman
His own brother
reading.correct: A fat German man
reading.explain: The speaker grumbles that this fat German must be the one who shoved him.

reading.ru: Ведь вы уже, конечно, не нигилист.
reading.question: What assumption does the speaker make about the listener's beliefs?
options: That he is surely no longer a nihilist
That he has become a devout monk
That he has joined the police
That he has become wealthy
reading.correct: That he is surely no longer a nihilist
reading.explain: The speaker assumes that the listener is, of course, no longer a nihilist, and presses him to answer frankly.

reading.ru: Ее тешили, ей поддакивали.
reading.question: How do those around this woman treat her strange fantasies?
options: They amuse her and go along with what she says
They mock her openly to her face
They ignore her completely
They report her to the authorities
reading.correct: They amuse her and go along with what she says
reading.explain: The text says that people amused her and agreed with everything she said, even though she may have realized they were only humoring her.

reading.ru: Презирали его, смеялись над ним, смеялись над его преступлением те, которые были гораздо его преступнее.
reading.question: How do the other convicts treat Raskolnikov in prison, despite being guiltier themselves?
options: They despise him and mock his crime, even though they are far guiltier
They respect him as their leader
They avoid him out of fear
They ask him for advice
reading.correct: They despise him and mock his crime, even though they are far guiltier
reading.explain: In the epilogue, the other convicts, who were far more criminal than he, despise Raskolnikov and mock his crime.

reading.ru: Это могло бы составить тему нового рассказа, но теперешний рассказ наш Окончено.
reading.question: How does the novel conclude, according to this final line?
options: By noting that a new story could be told about Raskolnikov's gradual renewal, but this story is finished
By revealing that Raskolnikov escapes from prison
By showing Raskolnikov's death in Siberia
By describing his wedding to Sonya in full detail
reading.correct: By noting that a new story could be told about Raskolnikov's gradual renewal, but this story is finished
reading.explain: The novel's famous closing line says this could be the theme of a new tale, but the present story is now ended.
